intro:
大屯山 Datunshan (1092 m) and 七星山 Qixingshan (1118 m) are the two highest points in 台北 Taipei City, towering on top of the 陽明山 Yangmingshan mountain range, a dormant volcano in the North of Taiwan's capital.

Originally established under Japanese rule, the area became Taiwan's first national park, later renamed Yangmingshan in honour of 王陽明 Wang Yangming, an influential Confucian scholar of the Ming dynasty. Today, the park is a popular place for cherry blossom, water buffalos, butterflies, bird watching and its hot springs.
route:
The hike begins at 關渡 Guandu MRT. From Exit 2, it's a short walk to the Taipei Art University. Behind the university, a path leads from {{1}} through the forest upwards to {{2}} 清天宮 Qingtian Temple, and seemingly endless stairs make you quickly gain altitude.

Around the 10-kilometre mark, the first section of the 臺北大縱走 Taipei Grand Hike continues mostly flat towards 二子坪 Erziping. Instead, turn right at {{3}} and follow a steeper trail. Rope sections guide you to the West and South peaks before Datunshan Main Peak emerges from the tall silvergrass.

Descend to {{4}} 二子坪 Erziping or continue along the Taipei Grand Hike for another 2.5 kilometres to {{5}} 小油坑 Xiaoyoukeng. You can end your hike here, or continue to Qixingshan.

The trail ascends along the north-western slopes of the mountain, passing steaming fumaroles, a scent of sulphur in the air. Steep stone stairs through towering silvergrass characterize the final push to the peak.

After crossing {{6}} 七星東峰 Qixing East Peak, follow a series of steps as the trail gradually leads down to 冷水坑 Lengshuikeng.
transport: The hike starts at 關渡 Guandu MRT (Red Line). Return from Lengshuikeng via bus S15 to 士林 Shilin or 108 to Yangmingshan Bus Station.

intro:
基隆 Keelung is a major port city in northern Taiwan. Due to its frequent rainfall — 3.7 metres per year — and its significant maritime role, it is often called Taiwan's "Rainy Port."

The first trading port was established in 1863, and the area's rich natural resources, such as gold and coal, helped it become one of the busiest in the world.

To the west of the port, 大武崙山 Dawulunshan overlooks 安樂區 Anle District. At its summit stands 大武崙砲台 Dawulun Fort, built in 1820 as a military base defending Keelung Harbour during the First Opium War in 1840 and the Sino-French War in 1884. The fort was later expanded during the Japanese colonial period and subsequently used by the Taiwanese military. Today a national historic site open to the public, its remaining structures stand as a testament to Taiwan's military history.
route:
Start at the bus stop at 大武崙沙灘 Dawulun Beach, a popular area with restaurants and a café overlooking the ocean.

The hike follows a series of steep stone stairs, gaining most of its elevation in the first 800 metres towards {{1}} Eagle Rock, a viewpoint offering sweeping vistas of 基隆嶼 Keelung Islet and Taiwan's northern coast.

An optional but recommended detour loops around Lovers Lake. Legend has it that if a couple crosses its {{2}} bridge while holding hands, they are destined to marry.

After exploring the lake, continue to Dawulun Fort, situated east of the lake. Behind it, the highest point is marked with a triangulation stone.

For the descent, retrace your steps but turn right onto {{3}} 海星步道 Haixing Trail, which leads down to {{4}} a temple along the main road. Turn left and follow the footpath between the road and the ocean to return to the starting point.
transport: The Keelung Coastal Shuttle bus stops at nearby 外木山 Waimushan. On weekdays, bus 305 also stops next to the trailhead.

intro:
Initially inhabited by the Ketagalan tribe, 基隆 Keelung was controlled at various times between the 17th and 20th centuries by the Spanish, the Dutch, the Ming and Qing empires, and the Japanese, with a brief French invasion attempt.

Due to its strategic location overlooking the northeastern coast, military structures have existed in the hills around Keelung since at least the Qing dynasty.

Modernised during the Japanese occupation in the early 20th century and later used by KMT troops after the Second World War, today 槓子寮砲台 Gangziliao Fort stands as a well-preserved remnant of Taiwan's military history. At 162 meters, 槓子寮山 Gangziliaoshan is the highest point of the hill.
route:
The {{1}} trail begins at the far side of 國立臺灣海洋大學 National Taiwan Ocean University, winding up concrete stairs through a pleasant green forest corridor.

After roughly one kilometre, it intersects with 景寮路 Jingliao Road. Here, turn right rather than left towards the fort. A short walk later, the summit of Gangziliaoshan is accessible via {{2}} a dirt trail on the right-hand side of the road.

The peak has only a small clearing, just wide enough to reveal views of the ocean and 基隆嶼 Keelung Islet.

Simply bagging the peak would miss the point of visiting Gangziliaoshan, so after returning to the road, head east until you reach the old fort, where you can explore the many trails and historic buildings.

Finally, a short dirt track descends to {{3}} an apartment complex. Follow the road to 海科館 Haikeguan or 八斗子 Badouzi Station.
transport:
Multiple buses run between the centre of Keelung and National Taiwan Ocean University. Bus 1579, which travels between Taipei and Badouzi, also stops there.

From Badouzi or Haikeguan Station, a short local train runs to 瑞芳 Ruifang on the historic 深澳 Shen'ao branch line.

intro:
Located on the western shores of 淡水河 Tamsui River in 台北 Taipei, 觀音山 Guanyinshan forms part of the 大屯山 Datunshan volcanic system, which also covers most of 陽明山 Yangmingshan National Park on the opposite side of the river.

The shape of its ridgeline resembles the goddess Guanyin – revered as the bodhisattva of compassion and mercy in Chinese Buddhism – lying on her back, giving the mountain its name. Numerous ancient temples add to its spiritual significance.

In the 1960s, students from the Military Police School built a path from 凌雲禪寺 Lingyun Temple to the highest of its 18 peaks. It is still known as 硬漢嶺 Tough Man Ridge today.
route:
The typical route is a loop from Lingyun Temple in the south. However, I suggest traversing Guanyin Mountain from the north, starting at the ferry terminal near 八里老街 Bali Old Street.

Walk 1.5 kilometres eastwards along the river. At {{1}} the Guanyin Road Intersection bus stop, cross the main street and ascend via a side road to a small temple, 牛寮埔福德宮.

From {{2}}, a trail winds up the north-eastern slopes of Guanyin Mountain. Ropes are available at some of the steeper sections.

After a strenuous climb, the trail emerges from the forest at the often-busy viewing platform at the summit. Turn around and enjoy postcard views of Tamsui, 北投 Beitou, and the Yangmingshan mountain range.

Continue along the Tough Man Ridge Trail. The descent is more comfortable, with countless stone steps leading down to Lingyun Temple.
transport: Multiple bus routes serve Bali, including R22 from 關渡 Guandu MRT. Alternatively, you can take the public ferry from Tamsui, the final stop on the red line MRT. Bus O20 connects the trail's endpoint at 凌雲寺 Lingyun Temple to 蘆洲 Luzhou MRT (Orange Line).

intro:
Straddling the space between Jiufen and the northern coast, 基隆山 Jilongshan offers breathtaking views over a region steeped in Taiwan's mining history.

This hike begins near the remains of 水湳洞十三層遺址 Shuinandong 13 Levels. Built in 1933, this smelter was once Asia's largest refining facility, processing the abundant gold and copper ores found in the area.

Nearby, you can see the uniquely coloured 黃金瀑布 Golden Waterfalls, where a high concentration of pyrite and other minerals gives the water a striking yellow, almost golden hue.
route:
Start from Shuinandong bus stop along Highway 2. After a short walk up through the village, you will arrive at the trailhead {{1}}.

The ascent from this side is strenuous, with some rope-assisted sections, but the views towards the ocean make it all worthwhile.

From the top of Jilongshan East Peak at 467 metres, you can see the “golden” water mixing with the blue of the ocean at the poetically named 陰陽海 Yin Yang Sea.

Along the ridge, the trail continues towards the main peak of Jilongshan, offering views of the popular tourist village of 九份 Jiufen and the surrounding hills.

The descent towards Jiufen is less demanding. After passing the first shelter on the way down, turn right on an alternative trail that bypasses most of the stone stairs and avoids some of the crowds.

You may choose to end the hike in Jiufen, where Bus 1062 runs to Taipei. However, it is well worth extending the journey by hiking part of 燦光寮古道 Canguangliao Historical Trail to 瑞芳 Ruifang. Further stairways lead down to 瑞金公路 Ruijin Road, and after a short section alongside it, a path follows the Keelung River to the centre of Ruifang.
transport: Bus 791 or Taiwan Tourist Shuttle 856 serves Shuinandong. From Ruifang, buses or local trains go to Taipei, while Buses 856 and 886 return to the starting point at Shuinandong.

intro:
One of the "old" Xiaobaiyue which was removed in the 2006 update is 丹鳳山 Danfengshan, or "Phoenix Mountain", in Taipei's 北投 Beitou District.

Rumour has it that Danfeng was the name of a concubine of General Chen Jitang, a commander in Chiang Kai-shek's army who died in Beitou in 1954.

The peak is also known as 松葉山, or "Pine Leaf Mountain", named after the pine trees planted on it by the Japanese, and 大師山, or "Master Mountain", referring to the Japanese shrine carved into its rock in dedication to Master Kobo Daishi.
route:
From 奇岩 Qiyan MRT Exit 3, head east towards 奇岩公園 Qiyan Park and traverse it northwards. Cross 公館路 Gongguan Road and climb a few stairs through a residential area up to 奇岩路 Qiyan Road. Follow the road around a wide right-hand turn. On the right, an unmarked trail with some ropes leads up the hill {{1}}. It is a short but steep section which soon merges with a wider concrete path with some stairs.

Continue upwards towards a viewing spot with a large, red sculpture of a phoenix. Soon after, a small trail to Danfengshan forks off into the forrest on the left-hand side. It is marked on the ground with yellow paint {{2}}.

A track with some ropes leads to the a small rock platform. Despite its relatively low elevation, the peak offers beautiful views of the entire Beitou area below.

Near the Master's shrine, you can find the 幸福石 Happiness stone, an old stele with the inscription "台灣啊，要永遠幸福 Taiwan! May you be happy forever." engraved in it. It had been found nearby by historian 楊燁 Yang Ye, and was subsequently placed at this more prominent location.

Follow the trail downwards to reach the streets of 新北投 Xinbeitou. You can end your hike with a soak at 瀧乃湯浴室 Long Nice Hot Spring.
transport: The starting point is 奇岩 Qiyan MRT (Red line). The hike ends at 新北投 Xinbeitou MRT, which is a branch line of the Tamsui-Xinyi (Red) line.

intro:
紅淡山 Hongdanshan, known as the "Lung of Keelung City" or "Yangmingshan of Keelung," is a 208-metre-high hill close to the centre of Keelung and its "five bases": Keelung City, Keelung Port, Keelung River, Keelung Mountain, and Keelung Island.

It serves as the back garden for Keelung residents and offers a short, easy hike suitable for most visitors. Multiple well-maintained trails crisscross the area like a spider's web, with pavilions and gazebos as convenient rest stops. There are many cherry trees along the trail making this a popular place to visit during the cherry blossom season in early Spring.
route:
A small road leads to the trailhead, tucked between 寶明寺 Baoming Temple and a car repair shop.

The trail starts with a typical set of concrete stairs. After about one kilometre, turn left at {{1}} to follow the trail to an observation tower {{2}}.

Continue to the summit. On a clear day, there are good views on the city, the port and the coast below. Like Hollywood, Keelung's name is displayed in large letters on another hillside: K-E-E-L-U-N-G.

Begin your descent on the same trail, but turn right at {{3}} to head North. Follow this path and the connecting roads to the train station in 三坑站 Sankeng.
transport: Multiple buses serve Baoming Temple, but the trailhead is also just a short 1.5-kilometre walk from Sankeng train station, with regular local trains running between Taipei (40 minutes) and Keelung (5 minutes).

intro: 大崙頭山 Daluntoushan lies on the southern edge of the 陽明山 Yangmingshan mountain range. The shortest route to the summit begins at the parking lot and bus stop in 碧山 Bishan. This description follows an alternative approach, combining Daluntoushan and 劍潭山 Jiantanshan as part of the fifth section of the 臺北大縱走 Taipei Grand Hike.
route:
The trail begins south of Jiantan MRT Station at {{1}}, starting with a typical feature of hikes in Taiwan — an abundance of stairs. For most of the route, the hike follows the Taipei Grand Hike markers, though both 小百岳 Xiaobaiyue are located slightly off the main trail.

After climbing the first flight of stairs, keep left and head towards a large {{2}} radio tower. A {{3}} wooden platform offers views of 松山 Songshan Airport, which primarily serves domestic destinations and is known for its ATR 72 turboprop planes.

The triangulation marker atop Jiantanshan is somewhat hidden, located less than five minutes from the viewpoint, a few steps off the main trail.

Reconnecting with the Taipei Grand Hike, the trail follows the ridgeline with minimal elevation change for the next five kilometres. Upon exiting the forested area and beginning the ascent, it crosses the small 金龍產業道路 Jinlong Industry Road twice. After the second crossing, follow a trail climbing up from {{4}}. After a viewing point, you'll connect with the road again.

Aim for a trailhead at {{5}} and turn right at {{6}} just below Daluntoushan.

From the summit, descend towards Bishan, passing its many cafés, strawberry farms, and the popular 白石湖吊橋 Baishihu Suspension Bridge.
transport: The trailhead is located a short walk South from Jiantan MRT Station. The closest exit is 2. At the end of the hike, the S2 shuttle bus runs from Baishihu Suspension Bridge to Neihu, providing connections to various parts of Taipei.

intro:
五分山 Wufenshan sits atop 平溪區 Pingxi District in northern Taiwan, near the famous 十分瀑布 Shifen Waterfall. It is noticeable from a distance due to the large white domes of a radar station on its top. It is accessible by a road, making it a popular Xiaobaiyue for cyclists.

The hike described here begins on the opposite side of the mountain, near the 台灣煤礦博物館 Taiwan Coal Mine Museum.

新平溪煤礦 New Pingxi Mine opened in 1965, and coal had been extracted for just over 30 years until the availability of cheap imported coal rendered its operation economically unviable. The mine has since been converted into a museum, showcasing this fascinating aspect of Taiwan's indsutrial history.
route:
Walk from Shifen to the Coal Mine Museum. The trail starts behind the museum and ascends via stone steps through dense forest. After 1.4 kilometres, a small shrine marks an intersection {{1}}. Turn right and follow the signs to the 五分山氣象雷達站 Wufenshan Meteorological Radar Observatory.

Near the top, shortly after a gazebo lookout, you will reach a fork {{2}}. To the right, a short dirt path leads to the triangulation marker. The main path continues left to the observatory and paved road.

For the descent, retrace your steps to the shrine and hike down to 暖東峽谷 Nuandong Valley. Alternatively, continue on the trail from the summit (1.3 km) or follow the road from the observatory (5 km) to a bus stop on County Highway 106. Returning to the museum is also an option.
transport: 十分 Shifen Station is served by trains from 瑞芳 Ruifang on the Pingxi Line. Nuandong Valley is accessible by bus 603. If descending eastwards, Keelung Bus 846 runs along County Highway 106 to either Pingxi or Ruifang, with the closest stop at 李家祖厝 Lijiazucuo .

intro: 姜子寮山 Jiangziliaoshan is located in 七堵區 Qidu District in Taiwan's northern 基隆 Keelung area. It was added to the 2006 edition of the Xiaobaiyue list, replacing 瑪陵尖 Malingjian. On a clear day, both offer stunning scenery, but in terms of 360-degree views, Jiangziliaoshan has an advantage as it sits at a much higher elevation of 728 metres above Qidu, 暖暖 Nuannuan, 汐止 Xizhi, and 平溪 Pingxi districts of Keelung and 新北市 New Taipei City. A newly constructed trail, starting from a nearby bus stop and car park, has improved accessibility but also attracts larger crowds.
route:
Starting from a temple opposite Jiangziliao bus stop, the trail ascends to the peak over approximately three kilometres along well-maintained wooden steps and compacted soil paths. The observation deck at the summit provides 360-degree views across the entire region, including Keelung City, Taiwan's northern coast, and Keelung Islet. You can also see Wufenshan, the Xiaobaiyue featured in the previous chapter. On a clear day, even Taipei 101 is visible in the distance.

A worthwhile detour is 泰安瀑布 Taian Waterfall, a refreshing spot, particularly on a hot summer's day.

Turn right at a fork at {{1}} on the way back from Jiangziliaoshan. This leads to an alternative trailhead off 泰安路 Taian Road. Follow the road and a short section of 草濫古道 Caolan Historic Trail to a path near {{2}}.

Further on, the trail gains roughly 100 metres in elevation before descending back to the starting point.
transport: Bus F905 runs from Xizhi Station, which is about 20 minutes from Taipei Main Station by local train.

intro: 瑪陵尖 Malingjian is another peak that has been removed from the second and third editions of the Xiaobaiyue list. It is a pity, as it offers a fun, short hike from 七堵 Qidu, with scenic views from the summit. From the top, you can see the Keelung coast to the northeast and the city of Taipei in the opposite direction. On a clear day, Taipei 101 is visible in the distance.
route:
From Qidu Station, follow 崇智街 Chongzhì Road northward, first crossing a bridge over 基隆河 Keelung River before passing under Highway 1 into 自強里 Ziqiang Village.

Keep left and locate an unmarked trailhead near {{1}}. The trail ascends gently through a beautiful forest. You will gain altitude quickly and soon reach a small ridge. The path is partially overgrown but discernible. At a fork below the summit {{2}}, keep left.

Soon after, you will arrive at the peak, a small rocky platform rising a few metres above the trail. It offers panoramic views in all directions (just ignore a small industrial area down the hill). The reward for this short but demanding climb is a 360-degree vista over Qidu, Keelung, the northern coast, and as far as Taipei.

Retrace your steps to the fork at {{2}}. All three routes lead back down to 自強路 Ziqiang Road. Take the leftmost and longest option, which meets the road at {{3}}. From there, walk back to Qidu.
transport: Qidu Station is 30 minutes from Taipei Main Station by TRA local train, or slightly faster by Tze-Chiang or Puyuma express services.

intro:
Dajianshan is an enjoyable city hike in 汐止 Xizhi District in 新北市 New Taipei City. To distinguish it from other peaks with the same name, its full name is 汐止大尖山 Xizhi Dajianshan. The quickest ascent follows a relatively short and easy path of stone steps from 天秀宮 Tianxiu Temple, a popular spot to watch the sunset. The trail is especially popular during cherry blossom season.

This chapter describes an extended route featuring more challenging trails with some rope sections. It also passes multiple waterfalls.
route:
The hike begins at 世運村 Shiyun Village, a short bus ride or a 1.5-kilometre walk from Xizhi train station. Behind the bus stop, a road leads to the first set of stone steps. After a while, the trail reconnects with the road until reaching {{1}} Tianxiu Temple.

Save the main trail for the return journey. Instead, continue along the road. At a sharp left turn at {{2}}, a side trail leads to {{3}} 秀峰 Xiufeng Waterfall.

After this short detour, return to the road and follow it towards a large white building. This is 彌勒山天道清修院 Maitreya Mountain Tiandao Qing Monastery. Use the steps at {{4}} to connect to the main Dajianshan trail. Follow it Eastwards first towards {{5}} 四分尾山 Sifenwenshan, the highest point of the hike at 641 metres.

After the peak, turn back and take a right at {{6}} onto 茄苳古道 Qiedong Historic Trail, which leads to the three-tiered {{7}} 茄苳 Qiedong Waterfalls.

Following a short road section, another trail turns left into the forest at {{8}}. This path passes the Dajianshan Waterfalls and returns towards the monastery. Keep right at {{9}} to finally climb the peak, where a viewing platform and gazebo awaits you.

Descend via the main trail, following the stone steps down to Tianxiu Temple and back to Xizhi.
transport: Bus F911 runs from Xizhi Station to Shiyun Village or Tianxiu Temple (10 minutes).

intro:
南港山 Nangang Mountain is located in the eastern part of Taipei. It is best known for a group of peaks collectively called the 四獸 Four Beasts: 虎山 Tiger Mountain, 象山 Elephant Mountain, 獅山 Lion Mountain, and 豹山 Leopard Mountain.

To fully appreciate the extensive network of well-maintained trails and visit all Four Beasts, I recommend the following loop.
route:
Start at Exit 4 of 永春 Yongchun MRT Station and walk to a small {{1}} trailhead at the beginning of Songshan Road. The trail ascends towards {{2}} Tiger Mountain, followed by a paved road leading to a short trail that climbs to a viewing platform atop {{3}} Leopard Mountain.

Retrace your steps to the paved road and follow it in the opposite direction. The loop now crosses to the other side of the mountain. Aim for waypoints {{4}} and {{5}}, turning right at both forks before continuing towards {{6}} 九五峰 Jiuwushan ("Nine-Five" Mountain).

9-5 peak is marked by a large boulder painted white with red characters. Less impressive, beside a radio tower, is the summit marker of Nanangshan.

Further along, a short and slightly more challenging trail ascends {{7}} 拇指山 Muzhishan, offering spectacular views over Taipei from its rocky crag.

After descending, follow the signs towards {{8}} Elephant Mountain, and add a final detour to bag view-less {{9}} Lion Mountain along the way.

Continue on the trail to the viewing platforms on Elephant Mountain before taking the final stone staircase down to the {{10}} trailhead opposite 淨宗寺 Jingzong Temple. Walk across the park to reach 象山 Xiangshan MRT Station.
transport: Both the start and end points are accessible by MRT. Take the Blue Line to Yongchun and return via the Red Line from Xiangshan MRT Station.

intro: 土庫岳 Tukuyue is located in the northeast of 深坑區 Shenkeng District, 新北市 New Taipei City, close to the border of 南港區 Nangang District, 北市 Taipei City. It rises to an elevation of 388 metres.
route:
The hike begins near 中央研究院 Academia Sinica, the national academy of the Republic of China which was founded in 1928 in 南京 Nanjing and relocated to Taiwan as a result of the Chinese Civil War in 1948.

From the bus stop, follow 舊莊街二段 Jiuzhuang Street Section 2 gradually upwards and away from the outskirts of Nangang. There is a signboard to the right of house No. 124 and 萬景茶莊 Wan Jing Tea House, describing 更寮古道 Gengliao Historic Trail, one of five ancient paths connecting Nangang to Shengkeng and Shiding.

The trail has been refurbished and ascends over wide granite stairs. Dense tree cover provides shade, making it comfortable to walk even on a hot day.  

The trail briefly crosses a small road. Keep following the signs towards Tukuyue. Do not miss a left turn near {{2}}, which guides you to the final summit push.

At the top, a large gazebo with red columns and a tiled roof awaits, alongside a few benches and a summit stone in the shape of a truncated pyramid. The view towards Taipei is partially obstructed by trees.  

Instead of retracing your steps, continue downhill in a southerly direction towards another road, 土庫尖橋 Tukujian Bridge. You can follow the road entirely or take a shortcut at GPS coordinates 25.0171, 121.6335 towards 僑新新村 Qiaoxin New Village.
transport:
Bus stop 舊莊二站 Jiuzhuang 2nd Stop is served by multiple lines, such as S5 from Nangang Exhibition Center, the terminus of the Blue Line MRT, or 306 from 臺北市南港區公所 Nangang District Administrative Center.

For the return journey, take bus 912 from Qiaoxin New Village to Taipei City Hall.

intro:
大棟山 Dadongshan, is a prominent peak situated at the highest point of 龜崙嶺 Guilun Ridge.

It's one of five first-class triangulation points around the Taipei basin and a popular hiking destination for its convenient location close to both Taipei and Taoyuan.
route:
Start from 迴龍 Huilong MRT Station Exit 2 and walk towards {{1}} 新北武器公園 New Taipei City Arms Park, where military tanks and airplanes are on display.

From the park, a trail climbs through the forest as you pass a pavilion and makeshift exercise equipment on your way to the top of {{2}} 三福山 Sanfushan at 233 metres.

The route then follows a road, passing 青德宮 Qingde Temple. Nearby, a trail forks off on the right side of the road at {{3}}. Along this section, you'll pass {{4}} 鎮遠山 Zhengyuanshan (325 metres) and {{5}} 秋壇山 Qiutanshan (359 metres) before the trail meets a road on top of the ridge — this is the summit of Dadongshan.

The top offers extensive views of Taoyuan City and New Taipei City. On a clear day, Taipei 101 is visible.

Descend on a trail parallel to the road facing a Southern direction. A set of stairs connects with the road at {{6}}. Follow that road for a while, and reconnect with another trail at {{7}}. Alternatively, continue on the road which runs parallel to the trail.

You'll encounter the triangulation stones for {{8}} 石灰坑山 Shihuikengshan (373 metres) and {{9}} 望湖山 Wanghushan (350 metres) near an old Banyan Tree.

From here, continue South towards {{10}} 鶯歌石 Yingge Rock, a dramatic stone feature with a viewing platform overlooking 大漢溪 Dahan River.

Follow the stairs down the mountain, cross 中正一路 Zhongzheng 1st Road and the railway tracks. Then, turn right to 鶯歌 Yingge Station.
transport: The route above starts at Exit 2 of 迴龍 Huilong MRT (the final stop of the Orange line) and ends at 鶯歌 Yingge train station.

waypoints.name: End of trail, continue on the road

intro:
二格山 Ergeshan is located in 文山區 Wenshan District, 台北市 Taipei City. It lies near 貓空 Maokong ("Cat Hole"), one of the largest tea-growing areas in Taipei. It has also become a popular spot for enjoying the city's night scenery.

Ergeshan is a well-loved hike, and there are several ways to reach it. You can take a bus up to 草湳 Caonan for a shorter 5.8-kilometre loop, or complete the 12-kilometre-long Section 1B of the Taipei Skyline Trail to 石碇 Shiding.

In this chapter, we use the 貓空纜車 Maokong Gondola.
route:
From 指南宮 Zhinan Temple Station, follow Section 3 of Zhinan Road eastwards. Switch to the 岐山古道 Qishan Ancient Road trail where it runs parallel to the road. Aim for a trailhead at {{1}}, and use the stairs on the right to enter the trail. It is steep in places, with a few rope-assisted sections, but the trees offer good shade from the sun.

Eventually, the trail bends southward before making another right-hand turn near the summit of Ergeshan. As you emerge from the tree cover, you’ll enjoy 360-degree views over Taipei, with the green of the surrounding mountains and the blues of 翡翠水庫 Feicui Reservoir. A large wooden platform sits at the top, with the cornerstone positioned off to its side.

From the summit, the trail curves westwards, returning to Maokong. Follow the signs toward the gondola's upper station. Numerous shops and teahouses await here. A short detour to 小日子lazyday café is a worthy way to end your hike with drinks and snacks.
transport: The base station of the Maokong Gondola is located above the Taipei Zoo MRT Station (Brown Line). Begin your hike at Zhinan Temple and return from Maokong. Some gondola cabins have 48 mm thick glass floors. Known as "Crystal Cabins" or "Eyes of Maokong Gondola", they offer even better views of the lush green hills of southern Taipei.

intro:
南勢角山 Nanshijiaoshan and 天上山 Tianshangshan are prominent peaks in 新北市 New Taipei City.

Tianshangshan (also called "Emperor Mountain") is the highest peak in the Tianshangshan mountain range at 430 metres and offers expansive views of the Taipei Basin. It is a popular spot for viewing tung blossoms and fireflies in April and May.

Nanshijiaoshan, at 302 meters, is renowned for its cultural significance, most notably the 烘爐地南山福德宮 Hongludi Nanshan Fude Temple, which is a major pilgrimage site popular with businesspeople seeking wealth. Its unique "furnace-like" shape also contributes to its local name, 烘爐地 Hongludi.

Following Section 10 of the Taipei Sky Trail, both peaks can be combined in a point-to-point hike.
route:
From the trailhead, a short detour leads to {{1}} 長壽山 Zhangshoushan. Follow the trail Eastwards along the ridge passing {{2}} 平林山 Chengfushan and {{3}} 十八羅漢岩 Shibaluohanyan. Stay left at {{4}}, and continue past 石門內尖山 Shimenneijianshan, 石門內尖山東峰 Shimenneijianshan East Peak (398 metres), 三粒半 Sanliban and 三粒半大粒 Big Sanliban.

Pass by {{5}} 望月亭 Wangyue Pavilion to reach the top of Tianshangshan at 426 metres. The trail continues along {{6}} 五城山 Wuchengshan and {{7}} 文筆山 Wenbishan, circling around 彩蝶社區 Butterfly Community, passing {{8}} 五尖山 Wujianshan before reaching Nanshijiaoshan at 304 metres.

Continue to {{9}} Hongludi Nanshan Fude Temple before descending via 外挖子山 Waiwazishan to the {{10}} trailhead at Section 3, Anhe Rd.

From here, Taipei Skyline Trail continues to 新店 Xindian. Instead, turn left and walk to Nanshijiaoshan MRT station.
transport:
Busses 705, 706 and 707 from Dingpu MRT (Blue line) stop at 長壽山 Changshou Mountain bus stop next to the trailhead.

The trail ends near Nanshijiaoshan MRT (Orange line).

intro:
鳶山 Yuanshan, also known as "Three Gorges Kite Mountain", is located in 三峽區 Sanxia District, 新北市 New Taipei City. Its nickname derives from both its location — 三峽 means "three gorges" — and its kite-like shape.

The hike is popular for 180-degree views from Yuanshan Rock, which overlooks 桃園 Taoyuan and New Taipei City and has become a favourite photo spot.

It is also close to a pavilon housing 鳶山大鐘 Yuanshan Bell, a commemorative bell cast in 1985 to mark the 40th anniversary of Taiwan's liberation from Japanese rule. The original bell was erected by the Japanese army in 1923 to commemorate the Battle of Longenpu, it was later destroyed and buried. In 1985 a new rememberance bell was cast to commemmorate the 40th anniversary of Taiwan's liberation from the Japanese.

From the pavilon, the summit can be reached in a short in-and-out hike (1.3 kilometers one-way). Alternatively, many trails climb up from the southern shores of 鳶山湖 Yuanshan Reservoir, the shortest (800 meters) starts at .
route:
This chapter outlines a point-to-point hike from 大溪 Daxi to Sanxia along the entire ridgeline. Start at 情人谷 Lovers Valley bus stop. Follow the road around a right-hand bend over a bridge, then turn left onto Lane 565, Xinyi Road. Continue uphill, turn right at the end, and follow the trail to 娘子坑山 Niangzikengshan (240 m). From here, head east.

You'll pass {{2}} 烏塗窟山 Wutukushan (282 m) and {{3}} 五十分山 Wushifenshan (296 m) before reaching Yuanshan. Continue east to Yuanshan Rock, then descend to the parking lot. At {{4}}, fork off to a trail down to 三峽中山公園 Sanxia Zhongshan Park. Take a detour through 三峽老街 Sanxia Old Street before catching a bus on 復興路 Fuxing Road.
transport: Bus 263 connects Lovers Valley to Daxi Old Street (which you can reach via bus 5101 from 鶯歌 Yingge Station). After the hike, buses 705 and 706 go from Sanxia Old Street to Yongning MRT, while bus 940 connects to 府中 Fuzhong MRT in Taipei (both Blue Line).

intro:
獅仔頭山 Shizitoushan, or Lion's Head, is the highest point in 新店區 Xindian District, Taipei. As the name suggests, its peak resembles the head of a lion — if seen from the right angle and with a bit of imagination.

The area has a complex and often violent history involving the Atayal tribe, who are the original inhabitants, and various foreign powers — the Dutch, Han Chinese, and Japanese — who sought to exploit its main natural resource: the once-abundant giant camphor trees.
route:
The trail begins next to the bus stop on 新潭路三段 Xintan Road Section 3. It initially consists of comfortable wooden stairs leading to a flat open area called 觀獅坪 Guanshiping {{1}}, or "lion watching platform". As the name implies, you can see the distinctive outline of Shizitoushan covered in dense greenery. You may wonder how such a dramatic peak can be climbed without rock-climbing gear.

The answer lies in three chunky and steep wooden ladders. Love them or hate them, they are part of what makes hiking Shizitoushan fun. There are also rope-assisted sections to aid you over the steeper parts.

You'll first reach {{2}} 獅頭山前峰 Shizitoushan Front Peak, which, at 863 metres, is actually the mountain's highest point. At a fork, stay right {{3}} and follow the ridgeline past the Fangfan Monument to the main summit. Most views are found along the trail rather than from the peak itself.

On the return, worthwhile detours include {{4}} 隘寮遺址 Ailiao Ruins, {{5}} 小土匪洞 Small Earthen Cave, {{6}} 觀音洞 Guanyin Cave, and {{7}} 大土匪洞 Big Earthen Cave.

Continue northwards to an alternate trailhead at {{8}}, then follow the road south to another entry point {{9}} that reconnects to Guanshiping. From there, retrace your steps to the start.
transport: 新巴士獅仔頭山線 Tutan Holidays Line operates on weekends and public holidays from Xindian MRT (Beixin Road). The final stop, 新潭路三段275巷口 Lane 275, Section 3, Xintan Road, is right next to the trailhead.

intro:
Jinmianshan, also known as 鳥嘴山 Niaozuishan or "Bird's Mouth Mountain" due to its sharp, beak-like shape, and Xizhoushan are peaks in 桃園 Taoyuan's 大溪 Daxi District near 石門 Shimen Reservoir. They sit along a ridgeline extending East to 五寮尖 Wuliaojian in 新北市 New Taipei City.

Historically, the mountain was used as a quarry during the Qing dynasty, with its stones reportedly used in the construction of old Taipei City walls.
route:
From the parking lot follow the road until it turns into a trail that loops towards the top of Jinmianshan in a clockwise direction.

Turn left at {{1}} and aim for a fork at {{2}}. Here, you meet the long-distance Wuxi trail (TAO10). Turn right, and follow the trail in a South-Easterly direction.

There are multiple side trails branching off in all directions. Aim for {{3}} 十三份山 Shisanfenshan and {{4}} 白石山 Baishishan. Make a small detour to the historic {{5}} 東興 Dongxing bridge along 打鐵寮古道 Datieliao Historic Trail.

Carrying on past {{6}} Shiguikengshan, the trail leads over 百吉 Baji tunnel to {{7}} 頭寮山 Touliaoshan, {{8}} 內湳溝山 Neinagoushan and {{9}} 牛角湳山西南峰 Niujiaonanshan South West Peak. Manoeuvring through a maze of trail options, you finally reach Xizhoushan at 567 metres.

With occasional views down on 石門 Shimen Reservoir to your left, descend to its dam via {{10}} 新溪洲山 Xinxizhoushan.
transport: In order to combine both peaks in one hike, take a taxi to a paking lot near the trailhead — 大溪区金山路392巷268號, No. 268, Lane 392, Jinshan Road, Daxi District — or walk the extra five and a half kilometres from Daxi. From Shimen Reservoir, buses 503 and 5050 run to 中壢 Zhongli station in Taoyuan.

intro:
虎頭山 Hutoushan, is a hill located in 桃園市 Taoyuan City, a good example of an easily accesible urban Xiaobaiyue. That said, it was removed from the list in the 2006 second edition.

Hutoushan is a rolling hill without a prominent peak, and its actual summit is neither close to nor marked from the main trails of the more popular 虎頭山公園 Hutoushan Park.

The peak is, however, close to 虎頭山環保公園 Hutoushan Environmental Park, also known as 星星公園 Star Park, a popular place for night-time city views and date nights.

The hiking proposal below combines all of these areas in a loop course.
route:
From the bus stop enter Hutoushan Park near a scooter parking spot at {{1}}. A wide path lead up pass the triangulation markers for {{2}} Hutoushan Far South Peak and steeper stairs climb up to {{3}} Hutoushan South Peak.

There are various trail options exploring the park, but aim North towards {{4}} 三分山 Sanfenshan, {{5}} 五分山 Wufenshan and {{6}} 王公坑山 Wanggongkengshan before finding 成功路三段 Section 3, Chenggong Road at {{7}} near Hutoushan Environmental Park.

Turn right and follow the road to a small trailhead at {{8}} near a 龜山 Guishan Township boundary marker. The highest point of Hutoushan is about 100 metres to the right off the road.

Return along Chenggong Road to visit Hutoushan Environmental Park which, unlike the "summit", offers good views of Taoyuan and is a popular night time spot.

Further down along the road, turn left at {{9}} to find 虎頭山西峰 Hutoushan West Peak. Re-enter Hutoushan Park and return to the starting point. Alternatively, end your hike at one of the nearby bus stops.
transport:
The route starts and ends at 虎頭山創新園區 Hutoushan Innovation Hub bus stop. Multiple lines run the short journey from Taoyuan TRA station.

If you only want to visit Hutoushan Environmental Park and/or the highest point, bus 213 goes straight to 虎頭山環保公園 Hutou Mountain Eco-Park.

intro:
東眼山 Dongyanshan is located in Taoyuan's 復興 Fuxing District. At 1212 metres, it's the highest point in a National Forest Recreation Area of the same name.

Originally inhabited by Atayal Indigenous people, Chinese inhabitants of Taiwan violently pushed into the mountains to extract its rich camphor reserves. With the arrival of the Japanese in the late 19th century, Dongyanshan became a logging site — remnants of which can still be found today — for Japanese cedar and cypress. Finally, the area was designated as a Forest Recreation Park in 1991.

Besides its rich flora, Dongyanshan is also home to diverse wildlife including Formosan Rock Macaques, Red-bellied squirrels, Formosan hares and the rare and critically endagered Formosan pangolin.

There are easy and well-marked trails to reach the top from Dongyanshan visitor centre. A worthy point-to-point alternative is using 東滿步道 Dongman trail which links Dongyangshan with the adjacent 滿月圓國家森林遊樂區 Manyueyuan National Forest Recreation Area, which was opened to the public in 1988. It is particularly popular for its many waterfalls.
route:
Starting from the bus stop at Manyueyuan National Forest Recreation Area, follow the road past the visitor centre and locate the starting point of Dongman trail at {{1}}. The name "Dongman" is a portmanteau of "Dongyanshan" and "Manyueyuan".

{{2}} 處女瀑布 Chunu Waterfall, {{3}} 滿月圓瀑布 Manyueyan Waterfall and {{4}} 小妮瀑布 Xiaoni Waterfall are short but worthy detours.

Dongman trail is a long, challenging and steep hike with no cell service or water sources leading through a remote forest area.

Ignore a fork at {{5}} and continue on Dongman trail. At {{6}}, turn right onto 親子峰步道 Parent-Child Peak Trail towards the summit of Dongyanshan. From the top, follow the 東眼山志繼山步道 Dongyanshan Self-guided trail down to the visitor centre.
transport: Bus 807 runs from Sanxia to Manyueyuan. Taiwan Tourist Shuttle 506 connects Dongyanshan with Taoyuan's Daxi Bus Terminal.

intro:
石門山 Shimenshan — or Taoyuan Shimenshan to distinguish it from the 3237 metre high Baiyue of the same name — is located in 龍潭 Longtan District in 桃園 Taoyuan. 石牛山 Shihnioushan is situated on the border of 關西 Guanxi Township in 新竹 Hsinchu and Taoyuan's 復興 Fuxing District.

In between them lies the Eastern part of Shimen ("Stone Gate") reservoir, its name refering to the river mouth being flanked by Xizhoushan (Xiaobaiyue \#23) and Shimenshan. Completed in 1964, it serves multiple purposes including flood control, power generation, irrigation and water supply.

There are multiple trails to hike both Shimenshan and Shiniushan. This chapter describes a more challenging point-to-point hike visiting both of them, sometimes referred to as 雙石縱走 "Double Stone Walk". In fact, you could combine this route with \#21+\#23 to cover four Xiaobaiyue in an epic 26.5k adventure!
route:
From the bus stop, walk about 2 kilometres along a small road. After passing a temple and the parking lot, aim for the trailhead and keep right at {{1}} (turning left also brings you to the top and is easier and slightly shorter).

This is the most challenging part of the hike involving multiple rope sections and some scrambling. After keeping right at {{2}} and {{3}}, you will soon stand on top of Shiniushan enjoying the panorama from its prominent rocky peak.

Head North and keep left at {{4}}. After circling around the Southern shoreline of the reservoir, find the 小竹坑古道 Xiaozhukeng Ancient Trail at {{5}} and head for {{6}} 小粗坑山 Xiaozhukeng before reaching the, viewless, top of Shimenshan.

From here, the mountain is covered with a vast network of trails. The main option conitnues North and leads to {{7}} the prominent, main trailhead surrounded by countless food stalls.
transport: Bus 1820A runs from Taipei Main Station to Guanxi. 關金線B Guanxin Line B continues to 李樹下 Lishuxia bus stop. From Shimen Reservoir, buses 503 and 5050 run to 中壢 Zhongli station in Taoyuan.

intro:
十八尖山 Shibajianshan, also known as 18 Peaks Mountain Park, is the second-lowest of the Xiaobaiyue and located in 新竹 Hsinchu City.

Originally an indigenous hunting ground and later a designated Han gravesite, its function shifted dramatically over time. During the Japanese colonial era, it was transformed into a forest park, which opened in 1924. As part of its development, 33 Guanyin stone statues were introduced from Japan to appease restless spirits, with approximately 24 still remaining today.

The park later served as an air defense base during World War II and continued military use afterwards, resulting in numerous tunnels and concrete walls. Today, Shibajianshan is affectionately known as "Hsinchu's lung" for the fresh air it provides in the heart of the city.
route:
This route describes a combination of a few of the mainy side trails on Shibajianshan. It is designed to reach the highest point while also passing most of the remaining Gunayin statues.

If you're less interested in this kind of treasure hunt, starting from the trailhead at {{1}} 獅子亭 Lion Pavillon is a shorter and more straightforward way to visit.

Opposite the bus stop, turn into 寶山路145巷 Lane 145 Baoshan Rd and locate 博愛街5巷 Lane 5 Bo'ai Street, a small alley that runs between a school on the left and Shibajianshan on the right. At {{2}} turn onto a trail, then continue left at {{3}}, and connect with the main paved walkway at {{4}}.

Detour from the main path between {{5}} and {{6}}. Switch onto another side trail at {{7}} and walk towards a shelter. Cross the main trail, and continue for the final stretch to a wide area at the highest point of the hill. The summit marker sits on top of a small shelter opposite a red-roofed gazebo.

Loop around the top, aiming for another fork at {{8}}. Descend on this trail down to {{9}} Bo'ai Street, turn left and return to the starting point.
transport: Bus 83 connects Hsinchu train station with the Western trailhead at Jieshoushan Entrance stop. Alternatively, it's a short walk.

intro:
飛鳳山 Feifengshan, or Flying Phoenix Mountain, is a peak in Hsinchu's 芎林 Qionglin Township. It's a popular hiking destination near the city with multiple well-maintained trails offering panoramic views of Hsinchu and the Miaoli plains. It's also the furthest point in Taiwan from where you can see Taipei 101, but only with some luck on very clear days.

The typical hike of Feifengshan is a loop, either clockwise from 代勸堂 Daiquan Temple at or counter-clockwise starting at 修心宮 Xiuxin Temple.

The route here describes a much longer traverse called 飛沙縱走 Feisha Trail, named because it connects \textbf{Fei}fengshan and \textbf{Sha}kengshan.
route:
From the bus stop in Qionglin, follow road 竹24 past a large archway and proceed to {{2}} 觀日坪古道 Guanriping Ancient trailhead at Xiuxin Temple.

Pass {{3}} 石壁潭山 Shibitanshan, and turn left at {{4}} to the top of Feifengshan. You can complete the aforementioned loop and call it a day, or turn back to the fork and embark on a longer adventure.

You will soon reach {{5}} 中坑山 Zhongkengshan, which some consider the true summit of Feifengshan. Beyond here, the trail gets noticably quieter. Next up are 牛欄窩山 Niulanwoshan and 芎蕉窩山 Xiongjiaowoshan which is a quick detour off the main trail.

Cross a small road before making short detours to {{6}} 下橫坑山 Xiahengkengshan — the highest point of the trail — and 雞寮坑山 Jiliaokengshan.

Navigate to a trail at {{7}} which loops down to 橫山 Hengshan in a clockwise direction. It passes multiple minor peaks and merges with small roads at a few occassions. Aim for waypoints {{8}} and {{9}} to keep you on track.

Finally, cross a small bridge at {{10}}, then turn left to the main road and bus stop.
transport:
Bus 5614 runs from Hsinchu train station to Qionglin Junior High School and Xiangyuanwo Entrance which are the start and end point of the route described here.

Direct busses 1820 and 1820A also connects Taipei with Qionglin.

intro:
After landing on Taiwan in 1895, Japanese soldiers spread across the island, quickly subduing resistance in its heavily populated lowland areas. The aboriginal peoples in the central mountains put together much stiffer resistance, and it was not until 1913 that the last Atayal tribes finally gave up the fight.

Today, a small number of Japanese military outposts across Taiwan's mountains stand witness of this bloody history. One of the largest relatively intact structures is 李崠古堡 Tapung Old Fort or Lidongshan Fort whose four walls surround a 28 by 22 metre area on top of 1913 metre-high 李棟山 Lidongshan in 新竹 Hsinchu County.
route:
大混山 Dahunshan trail, also known as Linkong Corridor, starts off a small road (那羅至煤源道路) south of Highway 120 and leads into dense mountain forest.

Keep following the various Chinese-language markers towards {{1}} 大混山 Dahunshan at 1540 metres and 李棟山 Lidongshan.

You will find many remnants of Japanese fortifications like 八五駐在所 Bawu Outpost and the grave of Watanabe, a Japanese patrol officer.

Ultimately, the trail leads to Lidong Fort and the triangulation marker on top of Lidongshan.

Follow another trail northwards and descend to {{2}} a small collection of houses at the end of Highway 120 near 八五山大橋 Bawushan Bridge. The bus stop is a little further down the road.
transport:
Lidongshan isn't possible as a day tour relying solely on public transport.

Instead, arrange a driver to drop you off at the Dahunshan trailhead (GPS coordinates 24.6980, 121.2635) and aim for the last bus 5631 back from 鳥嘴部落 Niaozui Tribe to 內灣 Neiwan or 竹東 Zhudong.

Starting at popular 李棟山莊 Lidong Lodge (GPS coordinates 24.6896,121.3088) is an alternative. It shortens the hike but increases the driving distance.

intro: 獅頭山 Shitoushan straddles the border of Miaoli and Hsinchu. A combination of sandstone and faster eroding shale has created caves, many of which house religious sites, and a large number of Buddhist and Taoist temples can be found on either side of the mountain.
route:
Our trail starts through an old stone gate next to the bus stop on the Miaoli side. You'll soon reach a small road and the parking lots for {{1}} 勸化堂 Quanhua and 輔天宮 Futian Temple.

Buddhist 輔天宮 Futian Temple was built during the Japanese colonial era. It houses an altar dedicated to Hiroeda Otoemon, a Japanese police officer during World War II. Commanding a naval squadron of 2000 Taiwanese men in the Philippines, he was ordered to lead his troops into a suicide mission, but defied his superiors. Instead, he secured safe passage for his Taiwanese troops and commited suicide himself.

Turn left at {{2}} towards {{3}} 舍利洞 Sheli Cave Temple and {{4}} 開善寺 Kaishan Temple.

An eight-ton boulder sits in front of the Kaishan temple censer. It fell from a cliff in 2003, and miraculously missed both the temple and the censer. The event has been dubbed 「飛來石落石」奇蹟 “the Miracle of the Flying Falling Rock”, and the rock is now part of the temple complex.

The trail continues towards {{5}} 淩雲洞 Lingyun Cave Temple before turning back Eastwards, passing by the foot of a vertical rock face at {{6}} towards a viewing platform at {{7}} 望月亭 Wangyue Pavilion. A stone pillar indicates the border between Hsinchu and Miaoli counties, and a short, inconspicuous trail leads up to the summit (turning back in a Westerly direction).

On the way back, follow 獅山古道 Shishan Historic Trail. Pass 元光寺 Yuanguang Temple and {{8}} 海會庵 Haihui Nunnery, and take a right turn onto 六寮古道 Liouliao Trail near a pavillon at {{9}}. Visit {{10}} 七星神木 Seven Star Sacred Tree, a 400-year old Camphor tree and continue down to the Shitoushan Visitor Centre on the Hsinchu side of the mountain.
transport: From 竹南 Zhunan Station, busses 5805 and 5805A go to 獅頭山 Shitoushan stop in 苗栗 Miaoli. On the 新竹 Hsinchu side, bus 5700 runs to the Hsinchu HSR station from 獅山遊客中心 Shitoushan Visitor Center.

intro:
Wuzhishan, or Five Finger Mountain, is located in Hsinchu County, at the borders between Beipu, Wufeng and Zhudong Townships. It's famed for its ridgeline of five conjoined summits that resemble a giant hand. A significant religious sanctuary, the area serves as a spiritual heartland home to the historic Zaojun Temple and is celebrated for its "sea of clouds".

Most commonly done as an in-and-out hike from Zaojun Temple, the route below shows a point-to-point alternative crossing the full length of the ridgeline from 上坪 Shangping Village in Zhudong including an optional detour to 猴洞步道 Monkey Cave Trail at the end.
route:
From the bus stop, walk along a road to the trailhead at {{1}}. This section is less frequented than the more common ascent from 灶君堂 Zaojun Temple on the opposite end of the ridge. It contains multiple rope sections climbing towards {{2}} 小指峰 Xiaozhifeng "Little Finger Mountain" at 982 metre elevation. From here, the trail becomes easier and continues past {{3}} 無名指峰 Wumingzhifeng "No Name Finger Mountain" to the main peak of Wuzhishan, {{4}} 中指峰 Zhongzifeng or "Middle Finger Mountain".

Continue to {{5}} 食指峰 Shizifeng and {{6}} 拇指峰 Muzhifeng to collect all five of the fingers. The ridgeline is undulating, with many sections navigated via wooden stairs built over the tree roots.

For an extension, keep left at {{7}} and continue towards 大隘山 Daaishan. Turn right at {{8}} to head to a small road and temple. You could end the hike here and follow the road to the bus stop near Zaojun Temple, or continue back up to {{9}} and turn left towards another trail that connects with the famous Monkey Cave Trail. Its main attraction is {{10}} a 一線天 Thread of Sky, a 40 metre long crevice between two boulders, just wide enough to pass through.

At the end of Monkey Cave Trail, follow the road to Zaojun Temple.
transport: Busses 5630 and 5630A go from 竹東 Zhudong station to Shangping. On the other side, a bus runs from 五指山遊客服務中心 Wuzhishan Tourist Service Center (near Zaojun Temple) to Zhudong. It operates only runs on weekdays and requires prior reservation (035804422). Alternatively, a taxi ride will take about 30 minutes.

intro:
小百岳 Shaolaishan is a Xiaobaiyue in 大雪山國家森林遊樂區 Daxueshan Forest Recreational Area, part of Taiwan's famous 雪山 Xueshan (Snow Mountain) range. It can be reached in an easy 2 kilometer hike starting right behind the toll station (NTD 150 per person).

The hike is often combinded with 鳶嘴山 Yuanzuishan (Bird's Beak Mountain), an iconic peak with a 360-degree panorama on top. The following describes this version.
route:
The hike begins near the Yuanzuishan Trail Head bus stop on Daxueshan Road. After a steep first section, you will soon find rope sections as you climb towards the top of the forest cover. You are rewarded by panoramic views of the Xueshan mountain range. There are some exposed sections, and, generally, this option is not recommended for those afraid of heights.

After Yuanzuishan continue to Shaolaishan. The summit is covered in trees, but you can climb the observation tower to get more unobstructed views of the surrounding mountains. From Shaolaishan, the way down is easy on a wide and well-maintained trail to the Daxueshan Visitor Centre.

If you still have time and energy, continue on the main road for 250 meters before taking a trail towards Xiaoxueshan. It leads through a tranquil forest with many giant, old trees along a well-maintained and relatively easy trail up {{1}} 鞍馬山 Anmanshan (2.667 m, the summit itself is on military land and not accesible). The trail ends at Xiaoxueshan Visitor Centre. Keep in mind that this adds around 9 kilometers and 1000 metres of elevation gain.
transport: Taiwan Tourist bus 889 runs from 豐原 Fengyuan District in 臺中 Taichung to Xiaoxueshan Visitor Centre, stopping at multiple trail heads along Xueshan Road. Seats are limited and reservation is required.

intro:
南觀音山 Nanguanyinshan ("South Guanyinshan") is a hill in 大坑 Dakeng, in the eastern part of Taichung's 北屯 Beitun District. At its summit stands a Buddhist temple belonging to the Maitreya Realm of Omniverse.

Near the entrance of the main temple building, a colourful sculpture greets visitors. Painted in shades of blue, pink, and gold, it features a distinctive third eye on its forehead.  This figure is the creation of Maitreya Emperor Chen Jinlong, who calls it 彌諦 Mi-Di, or Alien Baby—an intergalactic messenger bringing hope and enlightenment to humanity. According to him: "With a funny expression and a kind heart hidden, she will accompany you every day and let more good things happen to you."
route:
The hike begins near Dakeng Bridge, where a large golden sculpture of a hand stands next to a set of concrete stairs leading into a patch of forest. After the first flight of stairs, a dirt path begins meandering up the hill.

A short climb later, you reach the top, where another human-sized golden hand welcomes you. Fierce-looking stone sculptures stand guard around the temple, while golden statues gaze over the area from the rooftops. On the far side of the complex, a tower-like structure houses various Buddhist artefacts, and from its top, you can enjoy a view of the green hills of Dakeng.

Behind the temple, a road descends the mountain. Follow it until you reach a sharp right turn. Here, a trail forks off. Mostly composed of compacted soil, it has been reinforced in places with repurposed materials such as old tyres.

Along the way, you will encounter a few paths cutting down to the left, but keep to the right at each junction, aiming for an unmarked summit (297 m) near a makeshift altar.

Beyond this viewpoint, the trail begins to descend and soon transitions into a small road. It crosses a stream before leading to a bridge over 橫坑溪 Hengkeng Creek. After crossing the bridge, turn left to reach the main road, then turn left again to return to the starting point at Dakeng Bridge.
transport: The start and end points of this hike are at Dakeng Bridge bus stop, which offers various connections to and from other parts of Taichung.

intro:
暗影山 Anyingshan is located in Taiping District in Taichung. The name translates to Shadow Mountain, and it is also known as Black Mountain or 酒桶山 Jiutongshan (Wine Barrel Mountain).

There are two origin stories for its name. One claims it's due to the mountain's shape resembling a barrel. The more colorful legend is that famous 17th century General 鄭成功 Zheng Chenggong (also known as Koxinga) spent a cold night on this mountain while leading his troops to 國姓 Guoxing. Suddenly, an elderly man brought a load of wine for them to drink to keep them safe from the extreme cold. When Koxinga wanted to thank him in person the next morning, he was nowhere to be seen. The locals claim it was the Earth God, and therefore changed the name to "Wine Barrel Mountain".
route:
Start at 東汴國小 Dongbian Elementary School and follow 山田路 Shantian Road for 5.3 kilometer along a small mountain road covering around 500 meters of elevation gain along the West side of Anyingshan.

On the right side of the road, a trail begings heading up the mountain at {{1}}. A dirt path at first, it soon narrows and features a few very steep rope sections. This short segment is the most challenging part of the hike. Once you arrive at the ridge, turn left to reach the summit within a few minutes. There are some improvised benches and a good view on Taichung.

On the way back, follow the (much easier) trail along the ridge line. It connects with Shantian Road at {{2}}. Follow the road to get back to the starting point.
transport: Buses 287 and 288 run from Taichung to Dongbian Elementary School. Take a taxi to skip the long walk from and to the trailhead.

intro:
大橫屏山 Dahengpingshan stretches along the boundary between Taichung and Nantou counties.

The shortest routes approach the mountain from the east near 水長流 Shuichangliu in Nantou or from the west off County Highway 136 in Taichung. This chapter describes a significantly longer option that is accessible by public transport. Note that this is a strenuous trek with challenging, steep rope sections.
route:
The hike begins in 龜溝 Guigou, following a dilapidated forest road towards the ridgeline near Erzaishan (818 m). After leaving the road, enter a dense forest that will accompany you for most of the hike.  

Upon reaching the ridge, head north towards the summit. Thick foliage surrounds the path, limiting views, with only a few clearings offering glimpses of the surrounding mountains.  

Along the way, pass Far South Peak (1,010 m) and South Peak (1,047 m). The final 500 metres to the main summit involve additional rope sections and a few short rock scrambles.  

From the top, you can see the neighbouring hills and the vast, flat cityscape of Taichung in the distance. On the opposite side, a small boulder provides a vantage point overlooking Nantou County.  

If time permits, continue along the ridge to visit North Peak (1164 m) and Far North Peak (1107 m) before beginning the descent via the same route.  

Near a clearing overlooking Taichung, approximately 500 metres south of the main peak, turn left at {{1}}. This trail connects to an old forest road leading down to 國姓 Guoxing.
transport:
Both trailheads are accessible from Taichung via a transfer at 草屯 Caotun. From there, take buses 6653 or 6655 to 龜溝 Guigou and 國姓 Guoxing, respectively. There are also connections from and to 埔里 Puli.
It is possible to do this hike in a single day, but it requires good conditioning, planning and an early start.

intro:
九份二山 Jiufenershan is a 1,174-metre-high peak in 國姓 Guoxing, located in 南投縣 Nantou County. It lies south of 崁斗山 Kandoushan, where, on 21 September 1999, a landslide buried a village and a deer farm under 3.5 million tonnes of soil and rock, tragically killing 39 people and 300 Formosan deer.

The collapse permanently altered the landscape, forming two natural barrier lakes at the foot of the mountain.

It was triggered by the 921 Earthquake, a magnitude 7.3 event on the Richter scale. Unlike most of Taiwan's earthquakes that occur off the East coast, this one was caused by a fault line near the island's centre in 集集 Jiji and caused widespread devastation and loss of life throughout all of Taiwan.

Several memorials pay tribute to this tragic event, including one located at the base of Jiufenershan which also features a 倾斜屋 slanted house that has been tilted by the quake.

Another is the 921 Earthquake Museum in 霧峰區 Wufeng District South of 霧峰 Taichung, one of the most badly affected areas. It was built at what was formerly 光復國中 Guangfu Junior High School, which was destroyed when part of the school was uplifted by the fault during the earthquake. The deformed remains of its running track stand as a stark reminder to the destructive power of the earthquake.
route:
The trail is 1.6 kilometres one-way and begins beside a mountain road in front of a stele, near a distinctive red brick house (GPS coordinates: 23.9370, 120.8418). If arriving by bus, add 5 kilometres.

The first half of the trail follows a narrow, mostly overgrown forest road. There are rare places with views into the valley. After a rest area, a simple path, at times equipped with old wooden handrails, continues to the vistaless peak.

Follow the same way back.
transport: Bus 6657 from Puli stops 5 kilometres from the trailhead at 學校前 School bus stop.

intro: 貓囒山 Maolanshan is a peak in 南投縣 Nantou County, located on the northern shore of 日月潭 Sun Moon Lake. The area has played a crucial role in Taiwan's tea cultivation history. During the Japanese occupation, a black tea research institute was established on Maolanshan—today known under the lengthy name 行政院農業委員會茶業改良場 Yuchi Branch of the Tea Research and Extension Station. Its branch director, Arai Kokichiro, dedicated his life to the study and promotion of black tea in Taiwan.
route:
The hike begins near 龍鳳宮 Longfeng Temple bus stop. Take 中山路270巷 Lane 270, Zhongshan Road on the left, and follow it about 150 meters upslope to the trailhead. A signboard and a monument honoring Arai Kokichiro mark the entrance.

The trail starts with a short stretch of wooden stairs before reconnecting with the road. At every bend, you can catch sweeping views of Sun Moon Lake with 水社大山 Shuishedashan in the background. As you climb, the path winds past tea fields and through a forest of Japanese cedar, Chinese fir, and Ceylon olive trees. The latter display fiery red foliage in the fall, earning this section the name "Red-leaf Trail."

At the summit, you will find a weather station and a viewing platform. Nearby, a large rock marker stands beside the Maolanshan triangulation stone.

Descend the same way you came up.
transport: 龍鳳宮 Longfeng Temple has multiple bus connections across Nantou, including to 水里 Shuili and 埔里 Puli, both of which offer onward connections to Taichung. The trailhead is also near the Sun Moon Lake stop at the Shuishe Visitor Center, which is served by direct buses from Taichung HSR and TRA stations (bus 6670B), as well as from the Alishan Visitor Center (bus 6739).

intro:
集集 Jiji is a town in 南投縣 Nantou County. Situated along the 濁水溪 Zhuoshui River, it is particularly famous for its mountain bananas—apparently a favourite of the Japanese Emperor. You'll find shops selling all manner of banana-based products, and even a banana-themed tourist factory to visit.

Jiji is also the principal stop along one of the remaining Taiwan Railways Administration (TRA) branch lines—the Jiji line from 二水 Ershui to 車埕 Checheng. Originally built in 1922 to support the construction of the 明潭 Mingtan Dam and power plant west of Sun Moon Lake, the line remains a nostalgic and scenic route.

集集大山 Jijidashan sits above the town, overlooking 水社大山 Shuisheshan and Sun Moon Lake. On a clear day, you can see as far as 玉山 Jade Mountain.
route:
From the 上麻竹湖(隧道口) Shang Mazhuhu (Tunnel Entrance) bus stop, follow the mountain road to the Checheng trailhead at {{1}}. The trail ascends through a mix of bamboo, betel nut, and banana trees, providing ample shade from the sun. Just before the summit, the trail intersects with the road coming up from Jiji. At the top, you'll find a radio transmission station; the summit marker is located beside the main building.

For the descent, take the narrow service road down towards Jiji. Along the way, you’ll pass occasional mountain homes and scenic viewpoints. The road is also popular with cyclists—if you're tackling it on two wheels, beware of wet leaves that can make the descent slippery.
transport:
Bus 6279 stops at Shang Mazhuhu (Tunnel Entrance), next to a small parking area. Alternatively, walking from Checheng Station adds about 2.5 kilometres.

The hike ends near 大坪 Daping, with multiple bus lines connecting back to Jiji Station, roughly 4 kilometres away. There is also a direct service—bus 6333D—to Taichung (TRA and HSR stations).

intro:
水社大山 Shuishedashan is the highest peak in the 日月潭 Sun Moon Lake area in 南投縣 Nantou County. It rises from 伊達邵 Ita Thao on the eastern shore of the lake. Several trails lead to the summit, but it is a strenuous hike in any direction, gaining roughly 1400 metres of elevation, one reason it has been removed from newer versions of the Xiaobaiyue list.

Due to being covered in a dense forest, there are only a few partial views on the lake along the trail, and there is no view from the peak. However, the forest is beautiful in its own right.
route:
From the bus stop walk 2 kilometres to {{1}} the trailhead near the 九族文化村 Formosan Aboriginal Culture Village amusement park.

Ascend an overgrown and loosely marked trail through thick bamboo forest. The vegetation gradually changes with elevation until you reach an open space beside the summit marker at 2059 metres. The true summit lies 600 metres further along another trail.

For the descent, follow the easier 5.75 kilometer long main trail with its characteristic thick ropes. The observation deck at the 2.75 kilometer marker offers the best views of the lake.

The trail continues down through diverse vegetation zones. Eventually, you will reach {{2}} a fork where stone stairs descend to the two trailheads closest to Sun Moon Lake. Turn right for the 青年活動中心 Youth Activity Centre or left for Ita Thao.

A word of caution: the ascent described here is marked only with small, weathered plastic ribbons and may be difficult to follow, especially in fog. A round trip on the main trail is a safer and easier alternative.
transport:
Several buses go to the Formosan Aboriginal Culture Village. Alternatively, take the ropeway opposite the Youth Activity Centre trailhead (buses 6669 and 6669A).

The Ita Thao trailhead is a short walk from 伊達邵 Yidashao bus stop (line 6669).

intro:
桶頭山 Tongtoushan or "Barrel Head" Mountain, also known as 天望崎山 Tianwangqi Mountain, is located in 中埔 Zhongpu Township in 嘉義 Chiayi.

It lies at the heart of 石硦林場 Shilong Forest Farm, an ecological nature area encompassing 30 hectares of forest near the city of Chiayi which makes it a convenient destination to escape the city for some forest bathing.
route:
From the bus stop follow the road for 7.5 kilometres to the trailhead at {{1}}. Alternatively, take a taxi from Chiayi.

The trail is a relatively short 3 kilometre-long counter-clockwise loop combining forest roads, boardwalks and a short trail section near {{2}} to reach a wide open field with a viewing area on top of Tongtoushan. There is a white sculpture of the number 605, the elevation of the mountain, next to the summit marker.

At the end of the descent, the path follows the main road for a short section back to the starting point.
transport: Busses 7215 and 7301 go to 中埔 Zhongpu from Chiayi. Take a taxi to skip the long walk from and to the trailhead.

intro:
旗尾山 Qiweishan is a peak in 旗山 Qishan District in 高雄 Kaohsiung. It marks the southernmost extent of the 玉山 Yushan mountain range, which stretches 80 kilometres to Taiwan's highest point.

The route described here links the ''Banana Kingdom'' of Qishan with the ''Tobacco Kingdom'' of 美濃 Meinong. Qishan is renowned for its banana farms and a sugar factory that once produced up to 1500 tonnes of sugar daily before ceasing operations in 2022.

Meinong is Kaohsiung's largest Hakka settlement and was once Taiwan's leading tobacco-growing region, with fields spanning 2300 hectares in the 1970s.
route:
From the bus stop, cross the Qishan River using the pedestrian and bicycle bridge, which leads directly to {{1}} the trailhead.

You will quickly pass 北旗尾南山 North Qiwei South Mountain (86 m) and 北旗尾山 North Qiwei Mountain (113 m) as the trail continues up the ridgeline. Ropes assist at steeper sections, and you may need to scramble over some of the larger boulders.

Near the summit, the trail joins another path ascending from 竹寮巷 Zhuliao Lane via 941 partially uneven and steep stone steps. Follow the final (and steepest) section to the pavilion at the top of Qiweishan.

From the summit, enjoy 360-degree views of Qishan and, on clear days, as far as 北大武山 Beidawushan, Taiwan's southernmost 3,000-metre peak.

You may descend all 941 steps to end your hike early. Alternatively, continue along the ridge, passing {{2}} 福美山 Fumeishan (334 m) and {{3}} 人斗山 Rentoushan (389 m), the highest peak of the route. After passing a temple towards the summit of 靈山 Lingshan, turn right at {{4}} and descend Southeastwards to Meinong. Optionally, make a short detour to summit {{5}} Lingshan (364 m) as well.
transport:
Several buses run from Kaohsiung to Qishan Bus Station.

E25 returns to Kaohsiung from 雷音寺 Leiyin Temple.

intro: 大崗山 Dagangshan is situated roughly halfway between 高雄 Kaohsiung and 台南 Tainan, representing the highest point of the Dagangshan Scenic Area.
route:
Start at the bus stop in 九鬮 Jiujiu and follow a footpath along Fuan Road. Pass a large military complex opposite 大崗山如意公園 Dagangshan Ruyi Park. You will find numerous vendors selling tasty local produce, a common sight throughout the hike. From this point, the road begins to climb, passing several grand Buddhist temples. The trail follows the road, occasionally cutting across its bends via short flights of concrete stairs.

A brief but worthwhile detour leads to 天靈洞 Tianling Cave Temple, a Buddhist temple inside a small natural cave with a vast views at its far side.

Continuing along a narrow road, the route passes near Dagangshan’s highest point at 310 metres, currently inaccessible due to its location within a military facility. Near the summit, an exercise field equipped with makeshift fitness and stretching equipment appears. Opposite this, a short trail leads to Dagangshan's replacement summit marker at an elevation of 290 metres.

Descend the opposite side of the mountain, keeping right to join a trail of compacted soil winding through a bamboo forest. This path leads to a limestone gorge, one of the main attractions of the area. Only little light passes through the narrow opening and the forrest canopy at its top, creating a dramatic lighting at the bottom. These kind of formations are common in Taiwan, and sometimes referred to as 一線天 "thread of sky".

After exiting the gorge, conclude the hike by following the road down to 崗山頭 Gangshantou bus stop.
transport: Both Jiujiu and Gangshantou are accessible by bus (for example, line R70) from Gangshan, a railway station in northern Kaohsiung and the terminus of the red line Kaohsiung MRT. Gangshantou is also served by direct bus 8042, providing a connection to the Tainan HSR station.

intro:
壽山 Shoushan is a popular hill in 鼓山 Gushan District in 高雄 Kaohsiung City. It's a coral limestone mountain with an extensive cave system.

Shoushan was originally known as Dagoushan ("beating the dog mountain"), an approximation of the sound of Takow, the plains Aborigines name for the area. The Japanese changed it to Takao, taken from an area in Kyoto, the Mandarin prononciation of which gives Kaohsiung its current name. When Japanese Crown Prince Hirohito visited in 1923, the mountain was renamed Shoushan ("long life mountain"). Another name still used is Chaishan ("firewood mountain").

The mountain is best known for its large population of Formosan rock macaques monkeys (Macaca cyclopis). Early Western visitors coined the name Ape's Hill. Today, it's commonly called "Monkey Mountain".

For the most part, the macaques, coexist peacefully with humans. That said, watch your belongings, don't carry food openly and never feed wild animals!

Given its strategic location overlooking Kaohsiung Harbour and the Taiwan strait, Shoushan has been a military area and was only, partially, opened to the public in 1989. Today, large parts of the mountain are part of 壽山國家自然公園 Shoushan National Nature Park.
route:
There are four trailheads, all located on the Eastern side of the mountain: {{1}} 動物園登山口 Zoo Trailhead, {{2}} 台泥登山口 Taiwan Cement trailhead {{2}}, {{3}} Beishoushan Trailhead and {{4}} 龍泉寺登山口 Longquan Temple Trailhead.

Besides wide paths and well-maintained boardwalks, there are lots of rough trails and short-cuts zig-zagging across the mountain. While they are exciting to explore, note that some of them are steep and significantly more difficult!

Start from {{5}} Gushan District office LRT station and walk to the trailhead at {{1}}. Follow the trail to a viewing platform at {{6}} 好漢亭 Haohan Pavillon which is the official summit point. The true summit is inaccessible within a military area, the closest you can reach is a signboard at {{7}}.

Follow one of the many trails Northwards and descend to Longquan Temple {{4}} and walk to 內惟藝術中心 Newei Arts Center light rail station {{8}}.
transport: All trailheads are well connected. See above for some options.

waypoints.name: Gushan District Office light rail station
Access prohibited board below the summit
Newei Arts Center light rail station

intro:
女仍山 Nürengshan is a gem of a forest trail in the indigineous Shizi Township, a short drive from Fangshan near the Kenting National Park.

A challenging trail with some steep and fun rope sections makes up for the fact that there's no view from the peak. The journey is the reward here as you climb past beautifully curved trees, a dried-up riverbed and a deep, green forest full of monkeys and other wild life.
route:
The trail starts near the parking lot of a coffee shop named after the mountain (女乃山咖啡屋). The road soon turns into a trail, and the first rope section gives you a taste of what's to come.

A narrow, somewhat exposed path leads up to a riverbed. Follow the cairns marking the way. After a while, the trail begins to steeply climb up the hill.

The vegetation gets thicker, and there's no indication of how far the summit is away until, ultimately, a small clearing appears. There's a triangulation marker and a Taiwanese flag on top.
transport: Doable but inconvenient. Bus 1778 runs twice a day between Dahu (Taitung) and Fangliao. The closest stop is 1.2 kilometres from the trailhead; walking along the road can be a bit sketchy.

intro:
大山母山 Dashanmushan, or "Mother Mountain" was added to the 2017 version of the Xiaobaiyue list. It's an easy alternative to nearby 萬里得山 Wanlideshan which requires a permit for the Nanrenshan Ecological Reserve Area.

The mountain was used as a backdrop for the 1967 romantic movie Moonlight Serenade produced by Shaw Brothers, Hong Kong's largest film production studio.

The start of the hike is near Nanwan (South Bay) in Kenting, just off Provincial Highway 26. Behind the popular beach lies Maanshan, Taiwan's last active nuclear power plant.
route:
The trail is a straightforward hike along often dry forest trails, providing an interesting change of scenery to the lush green of so many other trails in Taiwan.

From the Highway, a narrow road leads up the mountain. At its end, in the middle of a Chinese cemetery, a dirt path begins meandering to the top.

The hike has a gentle slope and is relatively easy, with only a few rope sections. There is a triangulation point on the peak, and the vegetation clears enough to provide some views. The distinct shape of neighbouring 大尖石山 Dajianshishan and the Kenting coast can be seen below.
transport: The starting point of the hike is a short walk from 跳石仔 Tiaoshizi bus stop near Kenting's South Bay Beach. There are multiple lines with frequent connections.

intro: Lilongshan is the highest point on the Hengchun peninsula, and its only peak of more than 1000 meters. From the top, there are beautiful views of the Southern coastline. On a clear day, you can see the small island of Xiaoliuqiu 小琉球 in the distance.
transport: The Northern trailhead is 3 km from Yuantong Temple 圓通寺 bus stop. The Southern one is 1.5 km from Gulingxi 古苓溪. Both have frequent connections.

intro:
Kalabaoshan is a 2395 m high peak located a short climb off Highway 8 in Taroko National Park. It was added to the Xiaobaiyue list in 2017 replacing Zulunshan the entrance to which had been severly damaged by a typhoon.

Kalabaoshan is near Bilu Sacred tree, a 50 metre high, 3000 year old Lunta fir which has stood the test of time, surviving land slides, lighnting fires, disease and the construction of a busy mountain road right next to it.

Provincial Highway 8, also known as the Central Cross-Island Highway, connects Dongshi in Taichung with Xincheng in Hualien. It opened in 1960 after four years of construction.

After severe damage to the road from the 921 Earthquake and Typhoon Mindulle, the section between Guguan and Lishan remained closed for non-Lishan residents for 19 years, only reopening for limited public transport in 2018.
route:
The trail starts to the right of the public restroom at the rest stop above Bilu Sacred Tree. It climbs over a few stone stairs at first, but soon follows a steep forest trail up to the summit marker.

There are no views on top, but the forest is beautiful in its own right.
transport: Bus 1141 connects Hualien with Lishan. It occasionally performs unscheduled stops at sights like the Bilu Sacred Tree. However, time is not enough to do the hike, and there is only one bus per day.

intro:
初音山 Chuyinshan is a mountain off the East coast in 吉安 Ji'an near 花蓮 Hualien City.

There are two main trails approaching the peak from different sides of the mountain. A shorter one starts from the Northeast at the end of a steep road up to 華林園 Huanlin Garden monastery. The longer approach begins in the Southwest near 鯉魚潭 Liyu Lake.

Adding a bit of road walking, they can be combined into the point-to-point hike described here.

The trailhead is also close to the beginning of the 翡翠谷 Fei Cui or Emerald Valley which leads to popular swimming spots and 子母瀑布 Zimu waterfalls .
route:
Start at Rongshu 榕樹 bus stop, just before the road crosses over 木瓜溪 Mugua River. From here, turn right at {{1}} and follow the road up the mountain for about 5.5 kilometres. The trail begins near {{2}} and leads to the peak through the forest.

There is a wide space on top and views down to Hualien and the Pacific Coast.

Descend in the opposite direction. After about 1 kilometre, you will reach the monastery Huanlin Garden. From here, follow another windy mountain road down for 4.5 kilometres and walk to 好客藝術村 Hakka Art Village bus stop.
transport: Take bus 303 from Hualien to Rongshu 榕樹 or lines 1139, 1139B and 1139C from Hualien or 壽豐 Shoufeng.

intro:
Liyutan (Carp Lake) lies about half an hour inland from Hualien city, surrounded by mountains and hills on all sides.

It's a popular destination for water activities, but also offers multiple hiking trails.

Behind the South-Eastern shore lies 鯉魚山 Li\-yu\-shan. There's a narrow road leading up the back of the mountain to a relay station near the summit.

The more rewarding option is to climb through the pristine forest that stretches up from the shore.
route:
The main trails start opposite a small parking lot near the Southern end of the lake. There are various options with names like Fitness Training, Scenic Picknicking or View-Gazing Trail which can be combined in multiple ways.

The shortest option starts on the Hiking Trail, soon diverts left onto the Outdoor Leisure Trail which then converges into the Bird Watching Trail.

All tracks feature wooden stairs which can be slippery when wet, natural forest paths and a few metal reinforcements.

At the top of the Bird Watching Trail, it's a left turn and a few more minutes up to a resting stop atop the triangulation point. There's no view from the overgrown summit.

After continuing on the View-gazing Trail, a left turn leads onto the Fitness Training Trail which winds back down to the small road that encircles the lake. An alternative is completing the View-gazing Trail and doing a full circle of the lake.
transport: Buses 303 and 1139 from Hualien stop at South Liyu Lake Recreation Area and Liyutan bus stop, respectively. Both are a short walk from the trail head.

intro:
