火燒山 Huoshaoshan is a peak on 	綠島 Green Island, a volcanic rock off the coast of 臺東 Taitung in Southeastern Taiwan. Sources disagree whether it is the island's highest peak at 280 meters or the second-highest at 274 metres behind 阿眉山 Ameishan (276 m).

Originally inhabited by the Amis people, Green island earned notoriety for housing a penal colony for political prisoners during the White Terror period. Parts of this story are captured in the 2022 movie 流麻溝十五號 Untold Herstory.

Today, the prison camp and a memorial recognizing this part of Taiwan's history can be visited on the Northern part of the island.

Besides its dark past, Green Island is a popular travel destination, especially known for its diving sites.
route:
The trailhead is located near 朝日溫泉 Zhaori Hot Spring, one of only three salt water hotsprings in the world.

Follow a dirt road until it merges into 過山步道 Across Mountain Ancient Trail. Turn left and follow the stone stairs upwards. Meet the road at GPS coordinates 22.651373, 121.486945 and turn left towards the gate in front of a military complex. This is the closest you can get to the highest point of Huoshaoshan which lies inside a restricted area.

Turn around and follow the road to the Ameishan trailhead (GPS coordinates: 22.65622, 121.48607). The summit offers 360 degree views over the island.

Upon coming down, turn left and follow a different branch of the trail down towards the coast.

Follow the main road South until you reach the trailhead for the 觀海步道 Ocean Viewing trail (GPS coordinates 22.644660, 121.499702). Climb the stairs and turn left at the first branch. This connects back to the dirt road and the starting point of the hike.
transport:
Ferries connect Green Island with Taitung and Orchid Island. There are flights from Taitung using de Havilland Canada DHC-6 Twin Otter planes.

There is no public transport on the island. You may find a tourist shuttle or taxi, but the easiest option is to rent a scooter or bicycle.

intro:
65 kilometres off the Southeastern coast of Taiwan and 125 kilometres North of the Philippines' Batanes, lies an island known by many names. Today, 蘭嶼 Lanyu or Orchid Island are the most commonly used ones. The indigenous Tao people refer to it as Pongso no Tao ("island of human beings"), Ma'ataw ("floating in the sea") or Irala ("facing the mountain").

An older Chinese name is 紅頭嶼 Hongtoyu ("red head island") which refers to its mountain peaks resembling red human heads when illuminated by the setting sun. This image lives on in the name of its highest peak 紅頭山 Hongtoushan.

The indigineous people of the island are the Tao (or Yami) who are the only Taiwanese indigineous group with a maritime culture. In particular, they are known for their traditional fishing boats called ipanitika and tatara and the 飛魚季 Flying Fish Festival.

Lanyu had long been off-limits for visitors and tourists, a ban that was only lifted in 1967.

The island is also the location of Taiwan's only nuclear waste storage facility which has led to various protests over the years.
route:
The trail starts opposite 椰油國民小學, an elementary school on the West Coast of the island, about halfway between 開元漁港 Kaiyuan Fishing Port and the airport.

Follow the compacted soil path up the hill. There is a good view on the Western shores of the island and towards Taiwan. At GPS coordinates 22.047225, 121.518643 turn right and follow the trail into a dense forest.

1.8 kilometres later, you will a small clearing at the peak. The trees are small enough to allow for some views over the island and its coastline.

Follow the same path back.
transport:
Ferries connect Lanyu with Taitung and Kenting, and there are flights from Taitung.

There is no public transport on the island. Scooters are the best option to move around.

intro:
馬祖 Matsu, is an archipelago located in the Taiwan Strait, approximately 200 kilometres northwest of mainland Taiwan, but only 10 kilometres from the coast of Fujian Province in Mainland China. The two largest islands are 南竿 Nangan and 北竿 Beigan.

Named after the goddess 媽祖 Mazu, the patron deity of seafarers, legend holds that Mazu's body washed ashore on Nangan after she drowned while searching for her father at sea.

Matsu served as a crucial military outpost during the decades-long standoff between Taiwan and Mainland China, with massive fortifications, tunnels, and bunkers carved into the granite rock. Following the lifting of martial law in 1992, Matsu has gradually opened to tourism, offering visitors a unique blend of military heritage, traditional Fuzhounese culture, and dramatic coastal landscapes.

The islands are also home to a Xiaobaiyue, the Northernmost on the list, 雲台山 Yuntaishan which sits at 248 metres on top of Nangan island.
route:
Yuntaishan is a very short (400 metres), steep walk up an asphalt road from the nearest bus stop. There's a small military museum and a viewing platform on top. It's worth a visit, but not the main hike to recommend on Matsu.

For a slightly longer stroll with wonderful 360 degrees ocean views, hop on a boat to neighboring Beigan Island and visit 螺蚌山自然步道 Luoshan Nature Trail.

From 塘后沙灘 Tanghou Beach follow the road Eastwards to the 北竿塘后道沙灘 War and Peace Memorial Park and then further to the trail entrance.

Luoshan Nature Trail was once a secret path used by locals to pick oysters. It follows along the ridgeline, and there's a short rope section in the middle. There are multiple view points overlooking the villages, the neighboring islands and the runway of Beigan's small airport.

The trail, ultimately, descends to the shoreline near a rock formation known as "Confucius on the Sea".

Follow the same way back.
transport:
For Yuntaishan (on Nangan Island), take the bus to 陽明橋 Yangming Bridge.

For Luoshan Nature Trail (on Beigan Island), take the bus to 塘后沙灘 Tanghou Beach.

intro:
金門 Kinmen is an island off the coast of mainland China's Fujian Province.

After the Chinese Civil War, it remained under the control of the Republic of China, which considered it part of its 福建 Fuchien Province.

Between 1958 and 1979, Kinmen saw constant bombing by the People's Republic of China Liberation Army forces.

After decades under Martial Law, travel restrictions were finally lifted in 1994, and Kinmen has become a busy tourist destination with regular flights to the main island of Taiwan and a ferry link with Xiamen.

太武山 Taiwushan is the island's highest point. There are, technically, two peaks, one near the route described below (253 m) which is also referred to as 北太武山 North Taiwushan and Taiwushan itself (250 m) which is located at inside a military radar station.
route:
From 蔡厝 Caicuo bus stop, walk about 1.4 kilometres along the road to {{1}} 斗門 Doumen trailhead. The hike soon climbs over blank rock with the occasional foothold chiseled into the granite. Along the way, you will find open views on Kinmen's Northern coast and Xiamen across the strait in Mainland China.

At the end of the trail, you'll reach a viewing platform underneath {{2}} 倒影塔 "Reflection" pagoda which sits on top of a small cave. Connect to the road behind it, and turn left.

Find {{3}} the entrance of 蔡厝古道 Caicuo Historic Trail, and follow it to {{4}} a large granite stele from the Yuan dynasty.

From Yuan stele, a short, scrappy and unmarked trail leads around barbed wires to the triangulation stone which sits on top of a boulder. At the time of writing, entrance is prohibited. Check the latest regulations and don't trespass!

Stay on Caicuo trail for the the descent. After passing {{6}} 元履湖 Yuanli Pond, the hike ends at the starting point.
transport: The closest bus stop to the trail head is 蔡厝 Caicuo which is served by line 18A between Shamei and Shanwai. Depending on your starting point, other bus stops might be more convenient.

intro:
澎湖 Penghu, also known as the Pescadores (Portuguese for "fishermen"), is an archipelago of around 90 islands and islets located approximately 50 kilometers off Taiwan's west coast, roughly opposite the cities of 嘉義 Chiayi and 臺南 Tainan.

蛇頭山 Shetoushan, or "Snake Head Mountain," rises on Penghu's main island of 馬公 Magong. At just 20 meters, it ranks as the lowest of the Xiaobaiyue peaks. Despite its modest height, the mountain holds strategic significance due to its commanding position overlooking the harbor entrance.

The nearest settlement is 風櫃 Fenggui, a fishing village whose name derives from the sound of blowholes along the basalt coastline - a resonance likened to a "wind cabinet," a traditional Chinese organ. The village gained fame following the 1983 release of the film 風櫃來的人 The Boys from Fengkuei.
route:
From the bus stop, walk to 風櫃東漁港 Fenggui East Fishing Port at {{1}} and follow the narrow asphalt road north to a parking lot. A small marker notes Shetoushan's height at 2000 cm, while inscriptions on a nearby stele aptly translate 蛇頭山 as Shetou "Hill."

At {{2}}, a monument commemorates the 1908 sinking of a Japanese naval ship off Magong's coast, which claimed 200 sailors' lives after a fire in the ammunition depot triggered a catastrophic explosion.

A few steps further stands the 法軍殉職紀念碑 French Soldiers Memorial at {{3}}, an obelisk honoring the 200-300 French soldiers who perished from disease during the Sino-French War of 1885.

Beyond this, an inconspicuous plaque marks Taiwan's earliest European settlement. In 1622, the Dutch East India Company constructed a fort on Shetou Mountain. However, Ming dynasty forces expelled the Dutch from Penghu in 1624, driving them to retreat to Anping (present-day Tainan), where they built Fort Zeelandia. This stronghold fell to 國姓爺 Koxinga in 1662, finally ending Dutch occupation of Taiwan.
transport:
Penghu is accessible via frequent domestic flights from multiple Taiwanese cities. By sea, ferries operate from Chiayi, Tainan, and Kaohsiung.

Bus 51 runs from central Magong to 風櫃金王殿 Fenggui Jinwangdian. Taiwan Tourist Line buses stop at the nearby 風櫃牌樓 Fenggui Decorated Archway.
